questions: Are the rash spots itchy, painful, or neither?
Do you have any swelling, warmth, or redness in the left great toe or any of the other painful joints?
Do you have a fever or chills (even mild) along with the swollen, warm left great toe?
Have you ever had similar episodes of sudden joint pain/swelling in the past, and if so, which joint(s)?
Have you ever had your joint fluid tested during a swollen toe/knee/hip flare (or had blood tests showing high uric acid, rheumatoid factor, or anti-CCP)?
Have you ever had your blood tested for uric acid levels or had a joint fluid sample tested for crystals (and if so, what were the results)?
During the toe flare, have you ever noticed a reddish, shiny rash over the joint or tophi (firm white/yellow nodules) on the ear/olecranon/fingers?
Have you ever had the swelling in the left great toe occur suddenly at night or reach maximum pain within 24 hours?
Do you have any psoriasis (or a personal/family history of psoriasis or inflammatory bowel disease)?
Have you ever had your blood tested for inflammatory markers (ESR and/or CRP) or for rheumatoid factor/anti-CCP antibodies, and what were the results (if you know them)?
answers: Doctor: Are the rash spots itchy, painful, or neither? Patient: I don’t have any rash spots. My main issue is pain in my left great toe, hips, and knees that gets worse with activity and better with rest.

Patient: I’ve noticed some swelling and warmth around the left great toe, but I don’t recall significant redness. The hips and knees feel sore more than visibly red, and they’re worse when I’m active.
Patient: No, I don’t have any fever or chills. I’ve just had the swelling and warmth in the left great toe, and the deeper joint pain in my hips and knees mainly flares with activity.

Patient: I haven’t had sudden episodes like this before; it’s been a slow, progressive worsening over the past several years. It mostly starts with my left great toe and then my hips and knees become sore with activity.

I haven’t had my joint fluid tested, and I’m not aware of any past blood tests showing uric acid, rheumatoid factor, or anti-CCP results. If I’ve had bloodwork before, I don’t know what specific markers were checked.
Patient: No, I haven’t had a joint fluid sample taken, and I don’t remember any blood tests specifically for uric acid or whether crystals were checked.

Doctor: During the toe flare, have you ever noticed a reddish, shiny rash over the joint or tophi on the ear, olecranon, or fingers? Patient: I don’t recall any reddish, shiny rash over my toe joint, and I haven’t noticed any firm nodules like tophi on my ears, elbows, or fingers. My main complaint stays focused on the swelling and warmth at the left great toe and the deeper pain in my hips and knees with activity.

Patient: It doesn’t really happen suddenly at night; the pain and swelling have come on gradually and have been getting worse over the years, rather than peaking within 24 hours. When it flares, it tends to worsen with activity and improves with rest, especially as the day goes on.

Patient: No, I don’t have psoriasis, and I don’t think there’s any family history of it or of inflammatory bowel disease. My symptoms have mainly been joint pain and swelling that worsen with activity and improve with rest.

“I’m not aware of any ESR or CRP results, and I don’t remember ever being told my rheumatoid factor or anti-CCP antibody levels. If I had bloodwork in the past, I don’t know which specific tests were done or what the numbers were.”
